function: Above PHY: model-free RL's action is a binary user-access (preference establishing) flag feeding a three-sided user-satellite-destination matching game, not a power, beam or channel value (p. 7).
notes: Excluded as above_phy. Reason on p. 7: the AS 'needs to decide whether to provide data collection services to the user', i.e. 'whether to establish a preference relationship', the 'preference establishing decisions' (action xi in {0,1}, Eq. 28). The allocation is made by a non-learned three-sided matching game of users, access satellites and destination nodes under capacity limits (p. 6, p. 8, p. 9, p. 10; UoRA and SoRA, Algorithms 1 and 2). The objective is the sum of priorities of accessed users (p. 5). No transmit power, bandwidth, beam or channel value is learned (power is a given parameter, p. 3, p. 4), so the satellite exception of step 1.4 for learned power, resource or beam control does not apply: the problem is user association and access control. The paper says the RL helps 'predict and approach the complete network channel state information' (p. 5, p. 7), but its output is the binary preference flag rewarded by the completeness of the preference list (Eq. 29, p. 7), and no channel-prediction error is reported; results are matched users, AS revenue, user satisfaction, iterations and time versus greedy and random matching (p. 10-12). Reviewer may confirm that this is not area 2 or area 6.
